questions.question: Which of the following best describes how the article characterizes the term "sub-Saharan Africa" as a geographical region?
options: A non-standardised geographical region with a varying number of countries depending on the organisation
A precisely defined region with exactly 48 countries recognised by all organisations
A region that includes all 55 African Union member states without exception
A region that strictly excludes any country with territory north of the Sahara
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that sub-Saharan Africa is "considered a non-standardised geographical region with the number of countries included varying from 46 to 48 depending on the organisation describing the region."
Incorrect. The article explicitly says the number of countries varies from 46 to 48 depending on the organisation, so it is not precisely defined with exactly 48 countries.
Incorrect. The article notes that the African Union recognises all 55 member states but groups them into five distinct standard regions, separate from the sub-Saharan Africa definition.
Incorrect. The article explains that the term may include polities that only have part of their territory in the region, so it does not strictly exclude countries with territory north of the Sahara.

questions.question: According to the article, which of the following countries is excluded from the UN Development Programme's "sub-Saharan" classification?
options: Sudan
Nigeria
Kenya
South Africa
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the UN Development Programme applies the "sub-Saharan" classification to 46 of Africa's 55 countries, excluding Djibouti, SADR, Somalia, and Sudan.
Incorrect. The article does not list Nigeria among the excluded countries; Nigeria is generally considered part of sub-Saharan Africa.
Incorrect. The article does not list Kenya among the excluded countries; Kenya is part of East Africa and considered sub-Saharan.
Incorrect. The article does not list South Africa among the excluded countries; South Africa is clearly part of sub-Saharan Africa.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why the concept of "sub-Saharan Africa" has been criticised, according to the article?
options: It is viewed as a racist construction that separates Africa and overlooks common genetic links and regional diversity
It inaccurately includes North African countries that are part of the Arab world
It fails to account for the Sahara pump theory and the movement of flora and fauna
It was created by the United Nations without consulting African geographers
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that critics have described the concept as a racist construction intended to separate Africa, and that traditional racial taxonomy has overlooked common genetic links and regional diversity across the continent.
Incorrect. The article does not criticise sub-Saharan Africa for including North African countries; rather, it discusses how North Africa is grouped separately with MENA.
Incorrect. The Sahara pump theory is mentioned as an explanation for how flora and fauna left Africa, not as a basis for criticising the sub-Saharan concept.
Incorrect. The article mentions the UN geoscheme as one organisation that defines the region, but does not say the concept was created by the UN without consulting African geographers.

questions.question: According to the article, what role has the Sahara played since around 3900 BCE in relation to sub-Saharan Africa?
options: It has formed an effective barrier separating the Saharan and sub-Saharan regions, interrupted only by the Nile in Sudan
It has facilitated easy migration and trade between North and sub-Saharan Africa
It has been completely impassable, with no interruptions whatsoever
It has served as a unifying cultural region linking all African peoples
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that since around 3900 BCE, the Saharan and sub-Saharan regions have been separated by the extremely harsh climate of the sparsely populated Sahara, forming an effective barrier interrupted only by the Nile in Sudan.
Incorrect. The article describes the Sahara as an effective barrier, not as facilitating easy migration and trade.
Incorrect. The article says the barrier is interrupted by the Nile in Sudan, so it is not completely impassable.
Incorrect. The article presents the Sahara as a dividing barrier, not as a unifying cultural region.

questions.question: Based on the article, which of the following statements about Sudan's regional classification is most accurate?
options: Some international organisations include Sudan as part of North Africa, while geographically it is considered part of sub-Saharan Africa
Sudan is universally classified as part of sub-Saharan Africa by all international organisations
Sudan is excluded from both North Africa and sub-Saharan Africa classifications
Sudan is classified solely as part of the Arab world and not considered African at all
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that although Sudan is geographically considered part of sub-Saharan Africa, some international organisations include Sudan as part of North Africa.
Incorrect. The article explicitly notes that some international organisations include Sudan as part of North Africa, so it is not universally classified as sub-Saharan.
Incorrect. The article discusses Sudan's inclusion in both North Africa and sub-Saharan Africa discussions, so it is not excluded from both.
Incorrect. The article discusses Sudan's relationships with the Arab world but does not say it is not considered African at all.

questions.question: According to the article, how does the African Union's regional breakdown differ from the sub-Saharan Africa grouping?
options: The AU recognises all 55 member states grouped into five distinct and standard regions
The AU excludes all North African countries from its membership
The AU uses the same 46-to-48 country range as the UN for sub-Saharan Africa
The AU only includes countries fully south of the Sahara
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the African Union uses a different regional breakdown, recognising all 55 member states on the continent grouped into five distinct and standard regions.
Incorrect. The article says the AU recognises all 55 member states, so it does not exclude North African countries.
Incorrect. The article contrasts the AU's five-region breakdown with the varying 46-to-48 country range used by other organisations for sub-Saharan Africa.
Incorrect. The article indicates the AU includes all 55 member states, not only those fully south of the Sahara.

questions.question: According to the article, which of the following is true about the Nile's role in connecting the Saharan and sub-Saharan regions?
options: Navigation on the Nile was blocked by the Sudd and the river's cataracts
The Nile provided an unobstructed route between the regions
The Nile does not flow through Sudan
The Nile was the only barrier separating the two regions
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the Sahara forms an effective barrier interrupted only by the Nile in Sudan, though navigation on the Nile was blocked by the Sudd and the river's cataracts.
Incorrect. The article explicitly says navigation on the Nile was blocked by the Sudd and cataracts, so it was not unobstructed.
Incorrect. The article states the Nile flows through Sudan, where it interrupts the Sahara barrier.
Incorrect. The article describes the Sahara as the barrier, with the Nile as an interruption, not the Nile as the barrier itself.

questions.question: Based on the article, which of the following countries is listed as one of the six African countries not geopolitically part of sub-Saharan Africa?
options: Algeria
Nigeria
Kenya
South Africa
answer_explanations: Correct. The article lists Algeria as one of the six African countries not geopolitically part of sub-Saharan Africa, along with Egypt, Libya, Morocco, Tunisia, and Western Sahara.
Incorrect. The article does not list Nigeria among the six countries excluded from sub-Saharan Africa.
Incorrect. The article does not list Kenya among the six countries excluded from sub-Saharan Africa.
Incorrect. The article does not list South Africa among the six countries excluded from sub-Saharan Africa.
